metadata.scenario_context: A group of international students are organizing a get-well-soon visit to their classmate Lisa, who is recovering from surgery. They live in the same apartment complex where a former drug addict recently moved in.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada would like to have drug addicts as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Morocco would not like to have drug addicts as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest bringing chrysanthemums as a get-well-soon gift for Lisa
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Choose an appropriate gift that shows care and consideration
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it’s acceptable to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Emily
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Hana, I was thinking... for Lisa's get-well-soon gift, we should bring her some chrysanthemums. They're really cheerful and symbolize recovery. What do you think? 

Also, I've been wondering, would you feel comfortable living next to someone who's a former drug addict? I mean, I know some people would say no, but... I think it’s important to give everyone a chance.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hana
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums do sound nice, but maybe something more personal would show we care more? Like a cozy blanket or a book she loves... something that feels more *thoughtful*.

As for the neighbor, I don't know... I really think it's a concern. People with that background can bring a lot of uncertainty. I wouldn't be comfortable with that at all.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Emily
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about a cozy blanket or a book, but I still think chrysanthemums would be a great addition to show our support. They can really brighten up a room, you know? 

As for the neighbor, I get why you might feel that way, but I think it's important to remember that everyone deserves a second chance. Living next to a former drug addict doesn't have to be a negative experience... it could be an opportunity for understanding.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hana
shared_prefix.message:
I understand chrysanthemums can brighten a room, but I just feel a blanket or a book would be more *personal*... something Lisa can use during her recovery.

Regarding the neighbor, I appreciate your perspective, but I still think having a former drug addict nearby poses a risk. It’s hard for me to agree that it would be a positive experience.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Emily
shared_prefix.message:
I get what you’re saying about a cozy blanket or a book being more personal, but at the end of the day, it’s all the same. Whatever we choose, I'm sure Lisa will appreciate the thought behind it. 

About the neighbor... I don’t really see meaningful differences here. Live and let live, right? People figure it out. I think it’s all about how we approach any situation, and with experience, you can handle any situation that comes your way. Why not focus on what unites us instead?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

As for the neighbor, I just can't shake the feeling that it’s risky. I respect your view on uniting us, but I also believe in being cautious about our environment. It’s not just about the individual; it affects everyone around us.
